screens_reviewed: Two scroll captures of one route (app/audit/[placeId]/review.tsx): top (header, intro, chips, submit-status banner, Quick actions, Survey pages) and mid-scroll (Youth weighting cards, Access review section, footer action bar).
verdict: A dense, single-column review/submit screen that is structurally sound on iPhone: it renders a native stack header that owns the Dynamic Island inset, and the absolute footer correctly pads for the home indicator via insets.bottom. The main weaknesses are a visible state contradiction (a green 'Submitted' banner shown next to 'Still incomplete', '0 saved answers', and a warning that the audit still needs answers), and the entire screen hand-rolling tokens through the static light-only designSystem object plus inline style maps instead of Tamagui theme tokens or the shared ui/* primitives.

critical_issues.location: Top capture: 'Submitted' banner vs Quick actions warning + chips
critical_issues.issue: The screen simultaneously shows the success banner 'Submitted - This audit has been submitted and is locked for editing', the chips '0 saved answers' and 'Still incomplete', and the warning 'Context still needs required answers before this audit can be submitted'. A submitted+locked audit cannot also be incomplete with zero saved answers; these states are mutually exclusive and confuse the auditor about whether anything is actually saved.
critical_issues.evidence: image 13-audit-review.png; submitStatus banner derives from deriveSubmitStatus({pendingSubmission, hasSyncedSubmission}) (review.tsx:297-300) while the incomplete warning derives independently from incompleteStep/findFirstIncompleteStep (review.tsx:282-285, 542-547) and chips from answeredCount (review.tsx:286-295, 515-518) - nothing reconciles a 'submitted' status against an incomplete/empty draft
critical_issues.fix: When submitStatus === 'submitted', suppress the incomplete warning and the 'Still incomplete'/'0 saved answers' affordances (or render a read-only locked summary), so the banner and the body cannot disagree. Gate the incompleteStep paragraph (review.tsx:542) behind submitStatus !== 'submitted'.

improvements.location: review.tsx Chip / AnswerPill / Badge-like pills / SectionCard / Button blocks
improvements.suggestion: PACK header is 'design_system_components_used: (none)'. The screen hand-rolls a Chip (review.tsx:1076-1091), pill badges (review.tsx:1061-1071, 611-625), and section cards entirely from raw YStack/XStack + inline style, even though CORE ships components/ui/Badge.tsx with a DesignTone-based pill. Adopt the shared Badge/Card primitives so radius, padding, and tone stay consistent with the rest of the app and respond to theme/fontScale.
improvements.evidence: packs/audit-placeId-review.md design_system_components_used line; CORE components/ui/Badge.tsx; review.tsx:1076-1091

improvements.suggestion: Almost every color/font is read from the static `designSystem` constant (review.tsx:23, e.g. 345, 487, 500-509, 764-769), which lib/design-system.ts:453-460 documents as the light-only fallback for module-level constants. Sibling components (YeeStackHeaderTitle, tab layout) use the live useDesignSystem() hook. As written this screen will not switch to the dark palette when the auditor toggles theme; move color/font reads into the component via useDesignSystem().
improvements.evidence: review.tsx:23 import { designSystem }; lib/design-system.ts:447-460 (static set is light-only) vs useDesignSystem (lib/design-system.ts:501-510)

improvements.suggestion: Headings and labels use raw numeric fontSize (30, 22, 11) instead of Tamagui '$' font-size tokens, and these literals do not multiply by designSystem.fontScale the way YeeStackHeaderTitle does (core: YeeStackHeaderTitle.tsx:1344-1345). Auditors who raise the accessibility text size will not see these scale. Use ScaledText / $ size tokens or multiply by fontScale.

improvements.location: Mid capture: each review section header has its own solid dark 'Edit section' button, plus Survey pages step jumps, plus Quick actions 'Edit audit'
improvements.suggestion: There are three overlapping ways to jump into editing (Quick actions > Edit audit, Survey pages step buttons, and a solid primary 'Edit section' button on every domain card). The per-section solid dark button competes visually with the real primary CTA (footer Submit) and adds weight to an already long page; consider a lighter/secondary treatment for 'Edit section' so the footer submit stays the single dominant action.
improvements.evidence: image 14-audit-review-sections.png; review.tsx:663-681 (solid theme.accent=primary button) vs footer primary submit review.tsx:790-817

tamagui_notes: review.tsx mixes Tamagui shorthand spacing tokens (gap="$2", p="$4", px="$3") with raw numeric layout values from designSystem (paddingHorizontal: layout.screenPaddingHorizontal at :767, rounded={designSystem.radii.lg} at :994). Colors are pushed through inline style={{ backgroundColor, borderColor }} maps rather than theme tokens, bypassing Tamagui theming (review.tsx:691-694, 998-1002).

Section cards apply boxShadow via designSystem.shadows.card (review.tsx:1001) - a CSS string; this renders on web/RN-web but native iOS shadow may differ from the intended elevation. Visible cards in both captures appear flat/borders-only, consistent with the shadow not rendering natively.
Numeric font sizes (30/22/11) are not '$' tokens and do not pick up fontScale (review.tsx:503, 1007, 1027).
platform_notes: Safe-area top is handled correctly: app/_layout.tsx leaves audit/[placeId] headerShown:false (core _layout.tsx:1384) but the screen mounts its own native stack header via useYeeStackHeaderOptions/Stack.Screen (review.tsx:323-335), and the header 'Maple Library Plaza / Review and submit' sits clear of the Dynamic Island in both captures.

Home-indicator inset is handled: the absolute footer uses paddingBottom: insets.bottom + 12 (review.tsx:769), and the scroll content reserves footerHeight + 24 of bottom padding (review.tsx:494) so content is not hidden behind the bar.

Thumb reach: the primary 'Submit audit' CTA lives in the fixed bottom bar within easy thumb reach; good. In these captures it reads 'Submitted' and is disabled (opacity 0.6, review.tsx:796-797), consistent with submitDisabled.

Compact-fit uses lib/responsive-layout (useResponsiveLayout + getResponsiveContentContainerStyle, review.tsx:83, 493) rather than fixed widths, so phone padding (15/16) comes from PHONE_LAYOUT_TOKENS.
not_assessable: Whether the contradictory 'Submitted' + 'incomplete' state is a real runtime bug or an artifact of the screenshot fixture/automation seed data cannot be settled from the static pack; the store data feeding submittedAudits/syncQueue is not in PACK.

Exact WCAG contrast ratios (e.g. green 'Submitted' banner text on successSoft, muted-foreground labels on surfaceMuted) are estimates; none looked clearly below AA in the light capture so none are flagged as critical.
Dark-theme rendering (the static-token concern) cannot be confirmed visually from a light-only screenshot.
Native iOS drop-shadow rendering of SectionCard cannot be verified from a flat screenshot alone.
score_rationale: Solid, well-structured screen with correct iPhone safe-area and footer inset handling and proper responsive-layout usage, but it has one real, user-visible state contradiction (submitted vs incomplete) and a consistency gap: it ignores the shared ui/* primitives (PACK: none used) and reads the light-only static designSystem instead of the live theme hook, so it lands at solid-with-minor-problems rather than ship-ready.
